cards.back:
The answer to an addition.
The sum of 4 and 5 is 9.
cards.say: Sum. The answer to an addition. The sum of four and five is nine.

cards.back:
How much bigger one number is than another. It is the answer to a subtraction.
The difference between 9 and 4 is 5.
cards.say: Difference. How much bigger one number is than another. It is the answer to a subtraction. The difference between nine and four is five.

cards.back:
The answer to a multiplication.
The product of 3 and 4 is 12.
cards.say: Product. The answer to a multiplication. The product of three and four is twelve.

cards.back:
To share into equal groups.
12 divided by 3 is 4.
cards.say: Divide. To share into equal groups. Twelve divided by three is four.

cards.back:
All the amounts added together.
5 + 6 + 2 gives a total of 13.
cards.say: Total. All the amounts added together. Five plus six plus two gives a total of thirteen.

cards.back:
One of the symbols 0 to 9 used to write numbers.
The number 305 has three digits.
cards.say: Digit. One of the symbols zero to nine used to write numbers. The number three hundred and five has three digits.

cards.back: A whole number that can be shared into 2 equal groups. It ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
cards.say: Even number. A whole number that can be shared into two equal groups. It ends in zero, two, four, six or eight.

cards.back: A whole number that cannot be shared into 2 equal groups. It ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.
cards.say: Odd number. A whole number that cannot be shared into two equal groups. It ends in one, three, five, seven or nine.

cards.back:
A number in a times table.
20, 25 and 30 are multiples of 5.
cards.say: Multiple. A number in a times table. Twenty, twenty five and thirty are multiples of five.

cards.back:
A sensible guess that is close to the exact answer.
39 + 21 is about 60.
cards.say: Estimate. A sensible guess that is close to the exact answer. Thirty nine plus twenty one is about sixty.

cards.back:
To change a number to a nearby, simpler number.
38 rounds to 40 to the nearest 10.
cards.say: Round. To change a number to a nearby, simpler number. Thirty eight rounds to forty to the nearest ten.

cards.back:
What is left over after sharing equally.
13 shared among 4 gives 3 each and a remainder of 1.
cards.say: Remainder. What is left over after sharing equally. Thirteen shared among four gives three each and a remainder of one.

cards.back:
The top number of a fraction. It says how many parts we have.
In 3/4 the numerator is 3.
cards.say: Numerator. The top number of a fraction. It says how many parts we have. In three quarters the numerator is three.

cards.back:
The bottom number of a fraction. It says how many equal parts make the whole.
In 3/4 the denominator is 4.
cards.say: Denominator. The bottom number of a fraction. It says how many equal parts make the whole. In three quarters the denominator is four.

cards.back:
Different fractions that name the same amount.
1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent.
cards.say: Equivalent fractions. Different fractions that name the same amount. One half and two quarters are equivalent.

cards.back: The distance all the way around the edge of a shape.
cards.say: Perimeter. The distance all the way around the edge of a shape.

cards.back: The amount of flat space inside a shape, counted in squares.
cards.say: Area. The amount of flat space inside a shape, counted in squares.

cards.back: When one half of a shape is an exact mirror of the other half.
cards.say: Symmetry. When one half of a shape is an exact mirror of the other half.

cards.back:
The opposite operation.
Addition and subtraction are inverses. So are multiplication and division.
cards.say: Inverse. The opposite operation. Addition and subtraction are inverses. So are multiplication and division.

cards.back: To say which of two numbers or amounts is bigger, smaller or the same.
cards.say: Compare. To say which of two numbers or amounts is bigger, smaller or the same.

cards.back:
From smallest to biggest.
3, 8, 15, 21 is in ascending order.
cards.say: Ascending order. From smallest to biggest. Three, eight, fifteen, twenty one is in ascending order.

cards.back:
From biggest to smallest.
21, 15, 8, 3 is in descending order.
cards.say: Descending order. From biggest to smallest. Twenty one, fifteen, eight, three is in descending order.

cards.back:
Objects in equal rows and columns.
3 rows of 4 is an array that shows 3 × 4.
cards.say: Array. Objects in equal rows and columns. Three rows of four is an array that shows three times four.

cards.back: How heavy something is. We measure it in grams (g) and kilograms (kg).
cards.say: Mass. How heavy something is. We measure it in grams and kilograms.

cards.back: How much a container can hold. We measure it in millilitres (ml) and litres (l).
cards.say: Capacity. How much a container can hold. We measure it in millilitres and litres.
